agricultural: Agricultural land shows large, contiguous parcels with uniform texture and regular geometric field boundaries. It differs from tennis court by having no court lines or net and being crop-based rather than sports surface; golf course by lacking manicured fairways and sand traps; chaparral by being less dense and more regularly patterned than shrubland.
airplane: Airplanes appear as elongated metallic objects with distinct fuselage, wings, and tail, parked on hardstand areas. They are distinguished from runway by being discrete movable objects rather than linear pavement; parking lot by having aircraft rather than vehicles; harbor by having no water or docks and being land-based.
baseballdiamond: Baseball diamonds are characterized by their distinctive diamond-shaped infield with raised pitcher's mound, outfield grass, and surrounding dirt. They differ from tennis court by having diamond geometry rather than rectangular with net; dense residential by having sports field rather than housing units; buildings by having open sports infrastructure rather than roofed structures.
beach: Beaches appear as narrow, light-toned sandy strips along water bodies, often with visible wave patterns and shoreline curvature. They contrast with river by being coastal or lakeshore rather than inland waterway; chaparral by having sand rather than dense shrub vegetation; agricultural fields show crops rather than sandy shorelines.
buildings: Buildings are characterized by rectangular footprints with visible roofs, shadows, and regular spatial arrangements in urban blocks. They differ from dense residential by being commercial or larger structures rather than housing units; parking lot by being roofed structures rather than open vehicle storage; baseball diamond by having vertical structures rather than open sports field.
chaparral: Chaparral appears as dense, low, dark-green shrub vegetation with irregular edges covering hillsides, showing rough texture. It contrasts with tennis court by having wild scrub rather than maintained court surface; agricultural by lacking field boundaries and uniform crop rows; river by being land vegetation rather than water channel.
denseresidential: Dense residential areas show small housing units packed closely together with narrow streets, tiny yards, and uniform block patterns. They differ from sparse residential by having smaller lots and less green space; medium residential by having smaller lot sizes; buildings are larger commercial or institutional structures rather than houses.
forest: Forests appear as extensive areas with dense, tall tree cover, dark green canopy with rough, uneven texture and no visible ground. They contrast with dense residential by lacking buildings and roads; golf course by having natural tree cover rather than maintained fairways; agricultural by having natural tree cover rather than crop rows.
freeway: Freeways are wide linear strips of paved concrete with multiple lanes, clear lane markings, and overpass intersections. They differ from overpass by being ground-level continuous pavement rather than elevated structures; runway by being narrower with lane divisions and vehicle markings; river by being paved corridor rather than water channel.
golfcourse: Golf courses are large green areas with mowed fairways, lighter roughs, sand bunkers, and small water hazards. They contrast with agricultural by having scattered bunkers rather than uniform crop rows; forest by having maintained grass and open areas rather than dense canopy; chaparral by being manicured rather than wild scrub.
harbor: Harbors show calm water areas enclosed by docks, piers, ships, and cranes, with visible boundaries and artificial shoreline modifications. They differ from parking lot by containing water and vessels rather than vehicles; baseball diamond by having water infrastructure rather than sports field; storage tanks by having water and docks rather than metallic containers.
intersection: Intersections show cross-shaped road junctions with clear pavement markings, turn lanes, and traffic islands. They contrast with dense residential by being road features rather than housing blocks; freeway by being local junction rather than continuous corridor; parking lot by having road crossings rather than vehicle storage.
mediumresidential: Medium residential consists of moderate-sized houses on medium lots with regular spacing, tree-lined streets, and observable driveways. It differs from dense residential by having larger yards and more space between units; parking lot by having housing rather than vehicle storage; buildings are commercial structures rather than residences.
mobilehomepark: Mobile home parks show rows of small, narrow rectangular trailer units arranged in dense, uniform clusters with narrow access roads. They contrast with dense residential by having no permanent foundations or varied house designs; tennis court by having trailer units rather than sports court; storage tanks by having residential trailers rather than metallic containers.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated road segments supported by pillars, crossing above other roads or terrain, with visible ramps and shadows. They differ from freeway by being raised structures rather than ground-level pavement; runway by having pillars and elevation rather than surface pavement; chaparral by having elevated transportation structures rather than vegetation.
parkinglot: Parking lots are flat, open areas with visible rows of parked vehicles in organized lanes with painted markings. They contrast with harbor by having vehicles rather than ships and water; buildings by having open vehicle storage rather than roofed structures; medium residential by having parking rather than housing units.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, linear, dark water bodies with sinuous curves and riparian vegetation along banks. They differ from beach by being flowing water channel rather than shoreline; chaparral by being water rather than shrub vegetation; dense residential by having natural water feature rather than housing blocks.
runway: Runways are long, straight, wide paved strips with clear parallel markings, end zones, and no intersecting cross streets. They contrast with airplane by being pavement infrastructure rather than discrete aircraft objects; freeway by being wider with aircraft markings; buildings by having horizontal pavement rather than vertical structures.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential shows widely spaced houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with visible driveways and sparse road networks. It differs from dense residential by having much larger lots and more vegetation; chaparral by having houses and lawns rather than wild scrub; mobile home park by having permanent houses rather than trailer units.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic structures with domed or flat roofs, arranged in clusters, with visible shadows and connecting pipes. They contrast with buildings by being circular metallic containers rather than rectangular roofed structures; mobile home park by having industrial structures rather than trailer units; harbor by having metallic containers rather than water and docks.
tenniscourt: Tennis courts are rectangular playing areas with visible nets, court lines, and smooth surfaces, often with surrounding fences. They differ from dense residential by being sports courts rather than housing units; agricultural by having maintained court surface rather than crop fields; baseball diamond by being rectangular rather than diamond-shaped.
